timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: By noon the opera house belonged to Shawna, contained forty-seven people Vesper wanted alive, and had sold out a concert my wife hadn't agreed to give yet. "Nigga, how you sell tickets before the singer says yes?" I asked the manager. The manager, a round man named Paolo, held his hat against his chest.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "We heard she was coming." "Nigga, she came to look at curtains." "The city would pay to see that also." I looked at Shawna, then back at him. "This nigga got taste and no manners. Baby, come decide what part we keeping." Paolo nodded so eagerly I almost liked him before my wife had approved the performance. Shawna looked up from the stage.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "What time?" "Eight." "Get me a piano." Nigga, that was the entire negotiation. Rosa stood beside her in rehearsal clothes, looking out over the velvet seats. "I want the second song." "You can have three." "I knew this marriage would eventually benefit me." Tank sat in the front row with his feet spread so far nobody else could use it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He watched Rosa cross the stage like the theater had been built to solve his particular eyesight. "That nigga in love," I told Shawna. "That nigga has been in love. He just finally stopped looking surprised." Vesper's people occupied the dressing rooms upstairs. Assistants. Drivers. Two singers.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: An old cook who had brought her own knives because she didn't trust palace kitchens she couldn't insult personally. No prisoners in chains. People who had served one house so long that leaving it felt like stepping out of their own names. Vesper moved among them, checking rooms, carrying bags, doing little practical things with a seriousness nobody had ever applauded her for.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I let her work. Paolo caught me before I reached the door. Captain. One small difficulty. Nigga, don't introduce a large problem wearing a little hat. What is it? He pointed up. The stage curtain had caught halfway open. A man on the high walkway was pulling at a rope with both hands while another shouted that he was making it worse.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Below them, Shawna stood with her arms folded, waiting for the theater to stop taking rehearsal personally. Has it always done that? I asked. Only for important performances. Nigga, it better retire that habit today. I went up the side stairs. At the top, the two stagehands stared at my badge, then at my face. Captain, you don't have to— One leaned toward the other.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: That nigga fixes curtains too? Nigga, that man's wife downstairs. This nigga can hear you, I told them. And that part about my wife is why the curtain losing today. Show me what's caught. The first stagehand pointed with both hands. The other took the loose rope and got ready to help instead of spending the whole rehearsal admiring the volunteer.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The curtain's heavy edge had twisted around its guide. I got both hands on it, felt the stubborn weight, and pulled until the trapped fabric came loose with a long velvet sigh. The curtain opened. Below us, the whole stage filled with light. Shawna looked up at me from the piano. You showing off up there? Nigga fixing your sky.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She laughed and played the first chord. Her voice came up through the theater, clear and warm, and the two stagehands forgot to look impressed with me because my wife had begun doing her part. I let them. When I came downstairs, Paolo shook my hand as if we'd concluded a matter of enormous artistic importance. Perfect, he said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I looked at Shawna singing beneath the open curtain. Nigga, I know. Bastien met me at the stage door with Marcellus. Both wore dark suits. Both looked like they had decided to attend a funeral and were willing to arrange one if necessary. "Nigga, y'all dress like the portrait owes you money." "In a sense," Marcellus said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna came down the steps and straightened my collar. "Bring back the book." "That's all?" "And yourself. The book can't come to my show alone." I kissed her. "Front row." "Better be." The House of Nine Doors looked worse in daylight. Nigga, I had done quality work. One balcony still had tire marks across the marble. The gallery doors were boarded.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Somebody had placed flowers near the broken orchestra platform, and I couldn't tell whether they were mourning the musicians' equipment or the baron's dignity. Police guarded the front entrance. Black Mantle soldiers guarded the back. Zero's men. Different uniforms, same rich-man posture: shoulders wide because somebody else had promised to pay for the consequences.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Ardent stood between both groups looking like his afternoon had become legally confusing. He brightened when he saw me. "Captain." "Nigga, who invited the funeral jackets?" "The emperor claims an interest in the property." "I claimed it first. With evidence. And a Ferrari." A Black Mantle officer approached. Tall. Blond. A little scar beside his mouth.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He introduced himself as Colonel Severin Drake, forty-six, commander of Zero's household forces, like any of that was supposed to make me stop standing where I was. "The house is closed." I showed him my badge. "Open." "Your foreign rank has no authority here." Ardent straightened. "The captain acts with my full cooperation." Drake looked at him.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "You should be more careful with that." "Nigga, you should be more careful with your tone," I said. "This man been nothing but handsome and helpful." Ardent's younger officers tried not to smile. Drake stepped closer. "You enjoy making people love you." "Nigga, you make that sound difficult. Look at this man." I nodded toward Ardent. "Useful. Respectful. Helped my wife get home.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I liked him in twelve seconds. You been here longer and somehow getting worse." One of Ardent's officers coughed into his fist. Drake looked at him. "That nigga ain't your problem," I said. "You threatening the wrong part of the conversation." Bastien walked past us toward the front door. Drake moved to stop him. I caught Drake's wrist. Not hard enough to injure him.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Hard enough for his face to understand the rest of the sentence. "Let the old nigga walk." For a moment all the guns around us seemed to remember what they were for. Then Drake stepped back. "You have fifteen minutes." "Nigga, I was gonna take twenty.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You just made it thirty." Inside, the house smelled of smoke, polish, and rich people pretending damage wasn't permanent if they could afford repairs. Bastien led us through a long corridor into a portrait room I hadn't reached during the car chase. King Adrien Valcour hung above a fireplace in a gold frame. He wore the Crown of Midnight.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: For the first time, I got a good look at the thing we had crossed a sea to take from Zero. Black diamonds. White gold. Seven rising points. A blue stone at the front dark enough to look like midnight had learned how to shine. "That's a crown," I said. Marcellus smiled. "Yes." "Nigga, I was expecting a crown, but that's a crown.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Why nobody tell me the nigga had that much hat?" "We've discussed it several times." "Words, my nigga. You used words. Should've held your hands this far apart and looked worried about my neck." Bastien stood beneath the portrait. "His nose was wrong." Eliane's letter came back to me. The old royal face. The face whose nose was wrong. Marcellus studied the frame.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Bastien looked at the fireplace. I looked at both men looking until I decided we were giving the wall too much time to feel important. "Can I take it down?" "Carefully," Marcellus said. Nigga, I took it down carefully enough that only one corner of the wall objected. Behind the portrait was a shallow bronze door. No glitter. No dramatic ticking.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Just a family crest worn smooth where somebody's hand had once touched it often. Bastien took a key from inside his coat. I looked at him. "You had that the whole time?" "I knew where it belonged. I was afraid to leave her alone with what opening it would bring." "Nigga, she got company now." The key turned.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Inside sat a small black book, a red ribbon, and a child's drawing old enough that the paper had browned. A little boy had drawn a ship and a man with a crown too large for his head. Nico's name was written at the bottom. Bastien touched the edge of the paper with one finger. Marcellus lifted the book. Names. Payments. Promises. Not magic.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Worse, in a way: men writing down what they would do to other men if enough money reached the right table. Eliane's stitched marks matched the page corners. Marcellus found Rafael Sorel's name three times before I heard footsteps in the corridor. "Time," I said. Drake stood in the doorway with six men.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "You have recovered imperial property." "Nigga, you timed that beautifully." "Give it to me." Bastien closed the bronze door. Marcellus slipped the book inside his jacket. I picked up the portrait. "You want your old king back?" Drake raised his gun. I threw King Adrien Valcour at him. Nigga, the king finally did something useful after sixteen years on the wall.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The frame struck Drake across the shoulder. His shot went into the ceiling. I drove forward before his men could get a clear line, hit the nearest one hard enough to put him into a cabinet, and heard Bastien's pistol answer from beside the fireplace. Marcellus ducked behind a table. Ardent's officers shouted from the front hall.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The house filled with the same noise it had made two nights earlier, and I started to understand why rich people kept extra mansions. Drake pulled free of the broken frame and came at me with a knife. He was good. Not Gault strong. Not red-mask fast. Precise. Every movement meant something ugly and arrived without introduction. He cut my sleeve. I hit his jaw.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He drove me against the fireplace. I caught his wrist before the knife found anything I couldn't replace with a tailor. "You think they love you?" he hissed. "Nigga, you asking while we wrestle? Pick a mood." I slammed him into the mantel. The knife fell. Bastien fired over my shoulder at a man rushing the doorway.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I shoved Drake into the broken portrait and went after Marcellus. The front hall was blocked. The gallery was burning again. Nigga, that house had an unfortunate relationship with my visits. "Back way," Bastien said. "That's where his men are." "Not all the way back. The ninth door." I stared at him. "The wall door?" He nodded.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank's earlier threat about taking the whole wall came to mind, and I decided my brother deserved a chance to be right at a distance. We ran upstairs. The little blue door opened onto nothing. Nothing, in this case, meant twenty feet of air above the harbor, a narrow stone ledge, and a maintenance boat tied below. Marcellus looked down.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "I am sixty-two." "Nigga, you wearing it beautifully. Come here." I helped him through onto the ledge. Bastien followed. Gunfire struck the door behind us. I kicked it shut, looked at the boat, and called down to its startled driver. "Move left!" "What?" "Nigga, your other left!" He moved. We jumped. The boat rocked so hard the harbor tried to get in with us.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Marcellus landed against a coil of rope. Bastien hit the bench and rolled. I came down last, caught the boat's canopy, and tore half of it loose before my feet found the deck. The driver stared. "Captain Aiden?" "Drive, my nigga. Autographs when the roof stops shooting." The boat shot away from the house as bullets struck the water behind us.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Ardent's patrol launch cut across the harbor to meet us. His officers opened the way. Above, on the balcony I'd driven through before, Drake stood with blood at his mouth and the king's torn portrait tangled around one boot. I waved. Nigga, manners matter when you leave somebody's house. We reached the opera house at seven forty-three. Shawna was furious. Not because I'd been late.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Because I'd been early enough for her to see the sleeve. "You bleeding?" "Mostly architecture." "Aiden." "Nigga fought a portrait. Portrait lost. Little cut. Nothing interesting." "Then let your wife be interested before you start explaining the nigga in the frame." I held out my arm. Marcellus quietly held up the book behind me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "At least one of you came back with all his corners," she said. "Nigga, I came back with the useful ones." She checked it herself, cleaned it, and put a fresh shirt in my hands.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "You have twelve minutes." "To explain?" "To sit down and look like my husband." "Nigga, that's my strongest subject." "Then get an A and keep your feet out of the aisle." I did it in nine. Nigga, greatness respects showtime. The opera house filled until people stood along the walls. Vesper's household sat together in one balcony.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Ardent and his officers occupied another, their uniforms bright beneath the chandeliers. Gault arrived in a dark suit with no chain. When he saw me, he raised a hand and the whole row around him stood to make room. Tank sat beside me with Rosa's engagement ring box in his pocket, though she'd already said yes on the island. He liked carrying it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Said it reminded him he had managed one proposal without anybody shooting. The lights went down. Shawna walked onto the stage. No crown. No gun. No car. Just my wife, a piano, and a room that had no idea how quiet she could make it. She sang the first song without looking for me. That was what I loved about it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She wasn't borrowing courage from my face. She had brought her own. By the second verse, a woman behind me was crying. By the final note, even the waiters had stopped moving. The applause came a second late because everybody needed a moment to remember they had hands. Nigga, I stood first.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I stood so fast Tank stood with me on instinct, and the rest of the room followed like my wife's voice had pulled the city onto its feet. She found me then. Smiled. Everything I'd stolen, won, survived, or driven through felt small enough to put in a pocket beside that look. Rosa took the stage for the second song. Tank forgot to sit down.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She pointed at him once during the chorus, and the nigga actually touched his own chest like he needed confirmation she meant him. Mercedes leaned over from the next row. "That's your woman, nigga. Stop looking adopted by surprise." He laughed, embarrassed and proud, and I put an arm around his shoulders while the whole theater cheered her name.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "That's your nigga singing," I told him. "I know." "Then let the woman see you know." Tank raised both hands over his head and shouted her name so loudly Rosa almost lost the next line laughing. "There that nigga go," Mercedes said. "Whole damn balcony heard his relationship," Porsche answered. Nigga, so did Rosa.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She found her note again and sent it straight back to him. Upstairs afterward, Marcellus laid the recovered ledger beside Eliane's coat. Vesper read in silence. Payments to the harbor commander. Orders transferring the old king's properties before the fire. Names of men who had sworn loyalty at a funeral for people they'd helped kill. Then she reached the last page and stopped.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "What?" I asked. She turned the book toward me. A newer sheet had been tucked inside the old binding. Bell must have added it after acquiring the house. A record of the coming tournament's final wager. The Crown was to be awarded publicly. Then the winner would be invited aboard Zero's armored yacht for a private coronation. No winner was meant to return.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank stared at the page. "Nigga, they got a whole funeral scheduled after your trophy." I looked at Shawna standing in the doorway, still wearing the dress the city had just applauded. Then I looked at Vesper. "Aight," I said. "We gonna need a bigger after-party."
